short_description.text: Peter — Peter, brother of Andrew (MAT 4:18).
James — son of Zebedee (MAT 4:21).
Joseph — a Levite of Cyprian birth (ACT 4:36). Of the tribe of Levi.
Paul — the apostle Paul, at whose feet witnesses to Stephen's death laid their robes (ACT 7:58).
Timothy — a disciple and Paul's companion (ACT 16:1).
Aquila — a Jew native of Pontus with whom Paul stayed (ACT 18:2).
Priscilla — wife of Aquila (ACT 18:2).
Crispus — the believing leader of the synagogue in Corinth (ACT 18:8).
Apollos — an Alexandrian Jew mighty in the Scriptures (ACT 18:24).
Gaius — Paul's traveling companion from Macedonia (ACT 19:29).
Chloe — a believer in Corinth (1CO 1:11).
Stephanas — a believer whose household Paul baptized (1CO 1:16).
Forunatus — Paul rejoiced over him (1CO 16:17).
Achaicus — Paul rejoiced over him (1CO 16:17).
Achaia is a place named in Scripture (1Cor.16.15–Rom.15.26).
Asia is a place named in Scripture (1Cor.16.19–Rom.16.5).
Corinth is a place named in Scripture (1Cor.1.2–Acts.19.1).
Ephesus is a place named in Scripture (1Cor.15.32–Rev.2.1).
Galatia is a place named in Scripture (1Cor.16.1–Gal.1.2).
Macedonia is a place named in Scripture (1Cor.16.5–Rom.15.26).

who.text: God, Paul, Jesus, the Corinthians and Apollos.

where.text: Written from Ephesus to a wealthy port city.

what.text: Paul addresses divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, freedom, worship and resurrection in a divided Corinthian church. Genre: Epistle.
